text:
alex_g: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel selector roll (v2.14) we see a 12% drop in KV prefix hit-rate for the 4k model family. Spike correlated with a deploy at 22:03 UTC. Perf graph: https://grafana.redwood/graph?panel=kv_hit

maria_t: Ugh. Is this consistent across regions? any model-specific change?

alex_g: Primarily us-west and eu-west. Affected models: luminous-4k and lit-4k-quant. Non-4k models unchanged. Kernel change swapped a fused attention kernel for a tiled path — maybe hash alignment changed?

jordan: Could be batcher ordering interacting with prefix key normalization. Did we change key derivation in runtime? (e.g., include seq_len or tokenized prefix)

samir: I checked deploy logs — no explicit key format bump. Rolling back kernel restores hit-rate. So it's interaction, not data change.

perf-bot: probe results (5m windows): pre-roll avg_hit=0.71, post-roll avg_hit=0.62, delta=-0.09. sample queries:
```
# prometheus-ish
kv_cache_hit_rate{model="luminous-4k"}[5m]
```

maria_t: Two hypotheses: 1) kernel changed internal tokenization normalization order -> different prefix byte sequence 2) scheduling/batching changed request grouping so identical prefixes hit different buckets

alex_g: I instrumented the hash keys for a small subset. Example diff:
```
pre: key=hash(user:123|prompt_norm:"How do I") -> bucket=0x7a3
post: key=hash(prompt_norm:"How do I"|user:123) -> bucket=0x1c4
```
Seems order flipped for a small code path in the fastpath. Not all requests hit it.

jordan: That explains it. We never intended to include user id ordering in key. That's a bug in the kernel selector shim.

samir: Short-term mitigation: add backcompat normalization layer when computing prefix keys. Also consider seeding top-N prefixes after deploy to warm KV.

maria_t: For seeding, we should use a hybrid approach — replay top user-visible prefixes from recent traffic (obey PII filters) + small synthetic variations to exercise tiling paths. Scheduled job + an on-deploy quick seeder.

alex_g: I prototyped a seeding job that runs in two phases: 1) scheduled daily top-prefix replay (privacy-safe, scrubbed) 2) deploy-time targeted probe that synthesizes 2000 top prefixes with randomized suffix to prime caches. early results show +6-8% hit recovery.

perf-bot: sample seeder command:
```
./seeder --model luminous-4k --mode deploy-probe --count 2000 --tag deploy_probe_1742345678
```

jordan: Couple of safety notes: tag probe traffic so billing/metrics don't double-count; limit RPS to avoid autoscaler churn; watch KV eviction rates.

samir: Also add tracing: label seeder requests with header `X-SEEDER:deploy_probe` so we can correlate hit attribution in tracing.

maria_t: Action items:
- alex_g: PR to revert kernel selector bug + unit test for key ordering (ETA today)
- alex_g: push a canary seeder script to ops repo and tag traces (ETA tomorrow)
- jordan: add metric panel for seeder_hit_contribution and autoscale feedback loop (ETA 2d)
- samir: add rate limiter to seeder and make synthetic payloads privacy-safe (ETA tomorrow)

alex_g: I'll also add a short runbook step: rollback if post-roll hit-rate delta > -5% for 10m. Thanks all :thumbsup:

maria_t: Great work. postmortem if rollback needed, else ship followups.
